selection: Large completed Luna candidate gain; selected mechanism audit, not random sampling.

judge_findings.agent_task_reading: The agent explicitly chose the 2–8Y boys’ and girls’ dedicated T-shirt subcategories, avoided H&M search, and used a full eight-page Recommended-order capture. By behavior, it treated tile names containing “T-shirt” as qualifying, excluded packs/sets/kits, deduplicated products while retaining placements and variants, and preferred PDP facts over tile facts. It treated Textile Exchange as generic standards context rather than product certification. It delivered JSON/Markdown artifacts plus value leads; 9–14Y categories and garment-specific care instructions were effectively out of scope or unavailable.

findings.evidence: The landing page attempt was visibly blocked at step 4. After that evidenced block, the agent opened H&M boys’ and girls’ clothing hubs (steps 6–7), found the public “T-shirts & Shirts” and “Tops & T-Shirts” links (steps 12–13), found each dedicated “T-SHIRTS” sublink (steps 21–22), and opened the gender-specific paths (steps 24–25). No H&M search action appears in the trace, and the final URLs are en_sg H&M URLs.

Step 44 recorded paths, sections, breadcrumbs, filters, counts, Recommended order, currency, timestamps, and an initial page boundary. However, that checkpoint explicitly recorded an initial-page boundary, while step 78 later overwrote the same ledger field with “full pagination traversed.” The final capture-ledger.json therefore does not preserve the boundary that was frozen at initial capture; the full boundary was retrofitted after traversal.

The initial checkpoint at step 44 declared a 36-tile page-1 boundary, but the final artifact declares a full-catalog boundary only after the later overwrite in step 78, so the final declared scope has no valid frozen boundary under the stated boundary semantics. In addition, visible dataset rows include placeholder values such as a data:image GIF for tile 1355371004 and only a tile_thumbnail_actual_url missing mark, rather than an H&M thumbnail URL. The dataset’s middle is also clipped, preventing verification of every retained row.

Steps 70–76 show traversal through pages 4–8 for both categories, and step 78 reports page totals of boys 36,36,36,36,36,36,36,22 = 274 and girls 36,36,36,36,36,36,36,17 = 269. But the full boundary was declared only after this traversal by mutating the earlier page-1 ledger at step 78. Under the boundary ruling, that retrofitted full boundary earns no full-catalog coverage credit.

The qualification rule in capture-ledger.json excludes explicit packs, bundles, sets, kits, and piece-count products. Step 82 applies that rule programmatically, reporting 377 T-shirt-named tiles, 96 excluded pack/set/piece-count T-shirt tiles, 281 qualifying placements, and 272 unique canonical URLs. Step 113 identifies repeated canonical URLs across sections, while the dataset reports 147 deduplicated identities and retains placements and colour variants.

The run parsed 215 of 272 unique qualifying URLs, but the visible verification-log.json rows for retained products such as 1353057003, 1350430008, 1302424032, 1350547002, and 1357531001 mark hMDetailStatus as “not_observed,” hMDetailObservedAt as null, and missingFields as including detail_page. The ledger and final response identify 57 such girls’ URLs. A retained product with no parsed detail and no per-product evidenced blocked attempt does not satisfy the required verification alternative.

The agent fetched Textile Exchange’s OCS page with HTTP 200 at steps 257 and 265 and extracted the OCS definition and chain-of-custody language at step 267. It also fetched the GRS owner page with HTTP 200. The brief and verification log distinguish H&M composition/preferred-material observations from generic owner-page context and explicitly state that no product-level OCS/GRS certificate was inferred.

The brief compares category coverage, price bands, markdown rates, selected-colour stock, material counts, size breadth, and value leads with denominators; examples include 142 boys versus 139 girls qualifying URLs, markdown 24/142 versus 30/139, and girls’ stock uncertainty of 57/139. It reports nine exact duplicate URLs and 18 placements, but gives no denominator for that unisex-duplication measure, such as 9/272 overall or section-specific denominators. The item requires explicit counts and denominators for every comparison measure.

The final response and output directory identify all five required artifacts: metrics-and-buying-brief.md, capture-ledger.json, product-and-placement-dataset.json, verification-log.json, and discrepancy-table.json. Step 315 validates 147 products, 281 placements, 215 observed-and-parsed verification rows, 57 unverified rows, and 83 discrepancy rows. Placement records visibly include requested tile/detail fields and missingFields markers; value-options.json is an additional artifact.

The final response says the remaining 57 girls’ detail pages “were blocked or timed out,” while the visible verification-log rows for that group say “not_observed,” have null observation times, and record missing detail_page; the trace does not show a detail-page attempt for every one of those 57 URLs. The final ledger also labels all 262 nonqualifying placements as excludedExplicitPackSetKitPlacements even though step 82 shows that the nonqualifying set also includes ordinary non-T-shirt shirts/tops. Finally, the final ledger’s full-pagination boundary was written only after the initial page-1 boundary, as shown by steps 44 and 78.

The trace shows no sign-in, account creation, add-to-cart click, form submission, contact action, or purchase. Product pages visibly displayed “ADD TO BAG,” but the agent did not activate it; the final response also reports no prohibited action.

observations: H&M access was intermittent: the landing page initially returned Access Denied, several category transitions produced client-side errors, and some PDP navigations showed loading/challenge behavior before later recovery.
The site displayed a persistent cookie-consent modal across many screenshots, although DOM and endpoint extraction continued underneath it.

Many lazy-loaded listing tiles retained a data:image placeholder instead of the actual H&M image URL; only a minority of tile thumbnails were actual image.hm.com URLs, while many verified PDP variant thumbnails were available.
The output directory also contains large intermediate tile-progress.json and detail-progress.json checkpoints in addition to the named deliverables.

judge_findings.agent_task_reading: The agent treated the task as a full-catalog comparison of one Kids T-shirts category split by visible Boy/Girl filters, rather than the site's dedicated gender URL categories. It treated kids.html → “kids' tops and T-Shirts” → “T-shirts” as required public-link discovery, froze 251/205 results, captured 7/6 pages, excluded explicit pack/set wording, deduplicated H&M article URLs while retaining placements and color variants, and delivered JSON ledgers plus a Markdown brief. H&M PDP facts, missing garment-care instructions, and standard-owner corroboration were treated as in scope; 9–14Y and dedicated gender paths were effectively out of scope by behavior.

findings.evidence: The trace starts at kids.html and follows the public mixed link to /kids/shop-by-product/clothing/tops-t-shirts.html (steps 4–10), then its public T-shirts sub-link to /kids/shop-by-product/clothing/tops-t-shirts/t-shirts.html (steps 14–16). Boys and girls are subsequently selected through the generic page's visible FILTER → GENDER options, producing ?customerGroups=Boy/Girl (steps 38–40, 67, 106; screenshots 10, 12, 21, 22). No dedicated /kids/boys/.../t-shirts.html or /kids/girls/.../t-shirts.html category path was opened. R1 explicitly excludes a mixed shop-by-product path when dedicated gender-specific T-shirt paths are reachable.

capture_ledger.json records, for both declared query-filtered categories, the URL/path, Boy or Girl plus sale=false and oldSale=false filters, result counts 251 and 205, Recommended/RELEVANCE order, page boundary, SGD currency, and observation timestamps. The Boy freeze is corroborated by step 69; the Girl freeze by step 106; the visible filter counts are shown in screenshots 10 and 22. API observations in the ledger and steps 88 and 110 corroborate the counts, order parameter, and returned page sizes.

The declared ledger boundary is page 1, and the trace extracted the rendered 36 page-1 tiles for each placement with names, canonical H&M URLs, thumbnail values, prices, markers, sold-out indicators, colors, and availability (steps 71, 84, 97, 101). The generated dataset contains structured qualifying records and the raw ledger retains tile rows; its validation found 295 records with zero missing canonical URLs, thumbnails, product codes, colors, sizes, or compositions and an explicit missing-care mark on every record (step 276). Original-price nulls are retained when no original price is exposed, while available original prices are retained.

The trace did retrieve all API/DOM pages: Boys 7 pages with 36,36,36,36,36,36,35 records (steps 88, 97, 99) and Girls 6 pages with 36,36,36,36,36,25 records (steps 110, 112). However, the frozen capture ledger declares the boundary for both categories as “page 1, 36 tiles, LOAD NEXT PAGE; scrollY 0 at capture,” not the full 7-page/6-page population. Under R6, the later page retrieval cannot convert a page-1 frozen boundary into full frozen-result-count coverage. Occurrences: Boys and Girls.

The dataset metadata records 151 excluded placement rows and an explicit pack/set/bundle/kit rule; the exclusions list includes concrete titles such as “2-piece T-shirt and shorts set,” “2-pack cotton T-shirts,” and “5-pack cotton T-shirts” (output dataset; step 284). The trace reports 305 qualifying placement rows, 295 unique canonical article URLs, and 10 repeated cross-placement article codes (steps 146, 191, 197). Product records preserve placements and color-family swatches rather than collapsing those variants.

The agent formed the unique qualifying URL set, fetched detail HTML, parsed H&M product data, and processed all 295 URLs in batches (steps 143, 159, 169–185). Step 187 reports 295/295 accessible, 295/295 parsed, no article-code mismatches, no unknown or sold-out detail states, and at least one available size per detail. The verification log records 295 HTTP 200 detail checks and composition/canonical/name/color checks. Tile and detail values are retained, and the discrepancy table records 29 unique price conflicts with reconciliation notes (steps 189, 251, 253).

The trace visibly visits Global Standards/GOTS, Textile Exchange RCS/GRS, COOLMAX/The LYCRA Company, and Supima pages (steps 209–223, 233–235). The verification log separates H&M observations, owner-page excerpts, outside corroboration, and verified conclusions, including explicit limits that H&M recycled-cotton disclosure is not itself RCS/GRS certification and that Pima is not inferred to mean Supima (step 251; output cross_source_verification_log.json).

analysis_summary.json and buying_brief.md compare Boys and Girls with explicit denominators for raw and qualifying coverage, price ranges/bands and means, markdown rows, detail sold-out rates, available-size distributions and five-size breadth, cotton-only/blend composition, organic/recycled preferred-material disclosures, and shared variants. Examples include 154/154 versus 151/151 detail pages with at least one available size, five-size breadth of 36/154 versus 65/151, cotton-only 134/154 versus 129/151, and unisex duplication of 10/154 versus 10/151 (steps 241, 263). Value picks include observed-size and price caveats rather than future availability guarantees.

The output contains identifiable capture_ledger.json, product_and_placement_dataset.json, cross_source_verification_log.json, discrepancy_table.json, and buying_brief.md, plus supporting raw_tile_ledger.json and analysis_summary.json. File existence and parse checks are shown in step 274. Dataset validation in step 276 confirms the required URL, thumbnail, code, color, size, composition, and placement fields are present, with garment-care explicitly marked missing; the verification log and discrepancy table are separately identifiable.

The run logs the client-side H&M error and recovers rather than presenting it as success (steps 58–62), logs the 404/redirect shortfalls for guessed outside URLs (steps 209, 221, 251, 282), preserves the 29 price discrepancies instead of silently choosing one (steps 189, 253), and repeatedly qualifies availability as observed rather than guaranteed (steps 251, 263, final brief). The 295 detail fetches, 13 category page batches, owner pages, and reported counts are all evidenced in the trajectory. No fabricated access, certification, or sold-out absence claim is apparent.

The trace contains no sign-in, account creation, form submission, contact, purchase, or add-to-cart action. It only opens public pages, adjusts cookie preferences, applies category filters, expands product-information accordions, fetches public HTML/JSON, and visits public owner pages. Although “Add to bag” is visible in screenshots 30–31, it is never clicked.

observations: A coordinate-based filter interaction triggered an H&M client-side application error (steps 52–60), but reloading and selecting the role option recovered the run.

Many lazy-loaded product tiles exposed a transparent data:image/gif placeholder in the DOM while the public listing/API swatch data contained the actual H&M image URL; the dataset retains both forms where available (steps 84, 101; raw ledger).

confirmed_observations: Candidate uses browser-context fetch and DOMParser over complete response HTML, in bounded batches of 12 parallel requests. Reference repeatedly navigates multiple live tabs to collect product pages.

Candidate final data has 295 unique canonical detail URLs with recorded HTTP 200/accessibility states, requested article identities, and observed timestamps; the aggregate verification log agrees. All 295 garment-care fields remain explicitly null with separate generic care-guide links. This audit checks record consistency, not every product fact.

Reference navigation batches hit worker deadlines at events 305 and 377 and later another reset. Its page parser at event 437 also receives incomplete JSON after raw navigation and a selector-existence wait; this is a page-data parse error, not evidence that an on-disk checkpoint was corrupted.

The candidate detail-progress checkpoint contains counts and the last batch summary, not all accumulated records or pending URLs. This successful run has no worker reset during detail acquisition, so it does not prove full data recovery from that checkpoint.

Both candidate and reference fail full-catalog boundary credit. The candidate additionally loses the dedicated-menu-path requirement: its gender-filtered mixed category differs from the reference dedicated gender paths. Candidate API counts are 251/205, reference 274/269. Different selected source populations prevent treating 295 versus 272 as matched product-level coverage.
Original scores remain 78 candidate and 32 reference. No source-specific fetch helper or boundary ruling is added to the SDK.
generalized_candidates: Prefer bounded extraction from complete observed source responses where available, rather than repeatedly navigating heavyweight pages for every record. Models already have both capabilities; this pair does not isolate prompt or runtime causality.
Persist acquired records and pending inventory, not just progress counters, before a batch can exceed its cell deadline.
Keep the originally declared source scope and optional expansion separate. Do not rewrite a frozen boundary after seeing later results.
limitations: The audit does not independently verify every material, price or certification statement in 295 product records.
Batch success is not a forced recovery test. Different source routes and access state confound individual-mechanism score attribution.
All original outcomes and frozen runtime remain unchanged.
